chunks: Fearing that a great disaster is going to befall them.
ai.seo_question: What does it mean when the Quran says they fear a 'faqirah' will befall them?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse captures the psychological torment of the heedless who anticipate divine retribution yet remain in spiritual slumber, reflecting the concept of *ghaflah* (heedlessness) amidst the reality of *Qiyamah*. The 'calamity' (*faqirat*) is often interpreted as the piercing reality of death or the Day of Judgment that shatters their complacency, serving as a warning to believers to maintain *yaqazah* (wakefulness). This anticipation is not merely fear but a recognition of the inevitable accounting that awaits those who neglect their spiritual duties.
